$comment: Combination rules: which of the guide's components belong together for a human brain, decided once from the research in foundations/research/combinations.json. Every component sits on the same five axes (-1 to +1). A product's core (identity.json: character, plus an optional campaign goal) gives a target on those axes; the composer (tools/design/compose.mjs, npm run compose) scores every style x palette x pairing x hand against the target and these rules, and writes the winning combination into the campaign. Colours are computed from their CIELAB values; styles and typefaces are profiled below with the reason for each value. Change a profile or a weight here and every product follows.

styles.$comment: Each style's profile, from its own research (approaches/<id>/README.md, approach.json, art.json, motion.json).

humanist-minimal.why: Organic paper shapes and rounded corners, one idea with 40%+ empty ground, light ink line, spring motion, one hand note.

bauhaus.why: Elementary forms, heavy bars, one diagonal, bold grotesque, critically damped mechanical motion.

commercial-modernism.why: Mid-century advertising: confident lettering, two-stop gradients, smooth airbrushed forms, upbeat.

mid-century-modernism.why: Playful cut shapes, offset registration, earthy warm palettes, a little hand lettering.

scrapbook.why: Torn paper, tape, layered photos and notes: personal, collected, busy but light.

desi-maximalism.why: Frames within frames, pattern on every surface, many flat colours, painted lettering: celebration.

neon-surf.why: Bright, sunny, rounded type, airbrushed waves and glowing inks: loud and fun.

posterize.why: Photos cut to flat tone plates, heavy ink, strong contrast: graphic and bold.

doodles.why: Marker drawings around the message, loose lines, playful and light.

negative-space.why: 60-90% empty ground, one small object, quiet type, almost no motion.

typefaces.$comment: A pairing's profile comes from its display face's classification and style words (Henderson, Giese & Cote 2004 design dimensions) and its heaviest weight; the cues are averaged per axis. Body faces are chosen by the style for reading and do not move the profile.

colour.$comment: Per Wada colour from CIELAB. Brightness B = L*, saturation S = C*, both standardised over the 159 colours. Activity = Valdez & Mehrabian arousal (-.31 B + .60 S), potency = dominance (-.76 B + .32 S), both halved and clamped to -1..1. Warmth = C*/60 x cos(h - 50 deg), clamped (direction of Ou et al.'s colour heat factor; an approximation). A palette mixes its colours by area.

legibility.why: text contrast; below 4.5:1 a palette is never used for words

groundTextHueSimilarity.why: colour-pairs: pair preference and harmony rise with hue similarity

accentHueContrast.why: colour-pairs: a figure is liked more the more its hue contrasts with the ground

brandCloseness.why: fluency: the colours people already know the brand by

motion.$comment: How much a piece moves follows the target's activity (motion-arousal); how it moves is the style's motion.json.

byActivity.plan: Still, or one slow movement that ends still.
One movement at a time with a long still hold; loops of a few seconds.
Livelier sequences, still one mover at a time, never flashing.

hand.$comment: A hand face is used only when the style allows it and the target is clearly human (hand-and-machine).

lexicon.$comment: Brand character words (identity.json core.character) to axes. Unknown words are reported so they can be added here once.

goals.$comment: Optional campaign intent (npm run compose -- <product> <campaign> --goal <id>), added to the brand's own target.

launch.why: be noticed: arousal raises attention (motion-arousal, complexity)

rules.name: Agree on every axis
rules.rule: Style, palette and type sit close to the target and to each other on every axis. Axes the brand states strongly weigh more (0.5 + |target|).

rules.name: Type matches on potency and activity
rules.rule: The pairing is judged mainly on potency and activity.

rules.name: Ground and text: similar hue, strong lightness contrast
rules.rule: Body contrast 4.5:1 at least, 7:1 preferred; ground and text hues close.

rules.name: Accent contrasts in hue
rules.rule: The accent, the one figure, differs in hue from the ground.

rules.name: No disliked grounds by default
rules.rule: Dark yellow, olive and brown grounds are marked down unless the brand already owns the colour.

rules.name: Close to the brand's known colours
rules.rule: Palettes near the colours people know the brand by score up.

rules.name: One tension, moderate
rules.rule: At most one axis may differ moderately from the target (0.35-0.9), and only an axis the brand barely defines (|target| below 0.35): that is the piece's spark. Missing a trait the brand states is never a tension; two or more large differences, or one extreme one, are marked down.

rules.name: Complexity follows activity
rules.rule: Busy styles only for active targets; text zones stay calm in every style.

rules.name: Motion follows activity
rules.rule: How much moves is set by the target's activity (see motion).

rules.name: Hand only when human
rules.rule: A hand face only when the style allows it, and either the brand already owns one (its known signal wins over the average) or the target's hand axis is clearly positive.

rules.name: The style's own lists first
rules.rule: Palettes the style recommends and pairings it rates core score up; others are allowed when they fit better.
